summary: Hardened re-run: fetch + cite NCD defining criteria (WHO/Uganda-first), HTML-first, partial-return, never stall

definingCriteria.criterion: HbA1c (glycated haemoglobin)
definingCriteria.measure: HbA1c in whole blood (NGSP-certified / IFCC method)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: WHO/UCG-endorsed cut-off applied in Uganda. CAUTION: a Ugandan diagnostic-accuracy study (PLOS One 2022) found the optimal HbA1c cut-off in Black Ugandans was lower (~6.3% / 45 mmol/mol), and HbA1c is unreliable with the high local burden of anaemia, sickle-cell/HbS trait, malaria and HIV — prefer plasma glucose when haemoglobinopathy/anaemia is likely. HbA1c assay availability is limited outside referral labs.

source.guideline: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes — Section 2 (Diagnosis & Classification), concordant with WHO criteria
source.recommendation: HbA1c ≥ 6.5% (48 mmol/mol) is diagnostic of diabetes; performed by an NGSP-certified method standardised to the DCCT assay.

definingCriteria.criterion: Fasting plasma glucose (FPG)
definingCriteria.measure: Plasma glucose after ≥ 8 h no caloric intake
definingCriteria.threshold: ≥ 7.0 mmol/L (≥ 126 mg/dL)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: WHO cut-off used in Uganda (UCG / WHO-PEN). Ugandan validation study suggested a slightly lower optimal FPG (~6.4 mmol/L) for local Black populations, but the official threshold remains 7.0 mmol/L. Glucometer fingerstick is screening only — a venous laboratory plasma glucose is required to confirm.

source.guideline: WHO definition/diagnosis of diabetes (cited as the criterion applied in Uganda); ADA 2025 Section 2
source.recommendation: FPG ≥ 7.0 mmol/L (126 mg/dL); fasting = no caloric intake for at least 8 hours.

definingCriteria.criterion: 2-hour plasma glucose during OGTT
definingCriteria.measure: Plasma glucose 2 h after 75 g anhydrous glucose oral load (OGTT, per WHO method)
definingCriteria.threshold: ≥ 11.1 mmol/L (≥ 200 mg/dL)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: OGTT is the WHO reference standard but is resource-intensive (fasting + timed sampling) and infrequently performed outside referral/research settings in Uganda; FPG or random glucose is the practical first-line test at most facilities.

source.guideline: ADA 2025 Section 2 (test performed per WHO using 75 g anhydrous glucose), concordant with WHO
source.recommendation: 2-h plasma glucose ≥ 11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL) during a 75 g OGTT is diagnostic.

definingCriteria.criterion: Random plasma glucose with classic symptoms
definingCriteria.measure: Random (any time) plasma glucose PLUS classic hyperglycaemia symptoms (polyuria, polydipsia, unexplained weight loss) or hyperglycaemic crisis
definingCriteria.threshold: ≥ 11.1 mmol/L (≥ 200 mg/dL) + symptoms/crisis
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Most pragmatic diagnostic route at Ugandan facilities: a single random plasma glucose ≥ 11.1 mmol/L in a symptomatic patient is diagnostic and needs no confirmatory second test.

source.guideline: ADA 2025 Section 2, concordant with WHO; cited as WHO criteria in Ugandan literature
source.recommendation: In a patient with classic symptoms of hyperglycaemia or hyperglycaemic crisis, random plasma glucose ≥ 11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL) is sufficient to diagnose diabetes.

definingCriteria.criterion: Confirmation rule
definingCriteria.measure: Rule governing when a single abnormal result confirms diagnosis vs when repeat/second test is needed
definingCriteria.threshold: Two abnormal results required UNLESS unequivocal hyperglycaemia/symptoms
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: In the absence of unequivocal hyperglycaemia (i.e., asymptomatic, screen-detected patients), diagnosis needs two abnormal results — either two different tests obtained at the same time (e.g. HbA1c + FPG on one sample) or the same test repeated at two time points. A symptomatic patient with random PG ≥ 11.1 mmol/L is diagnosed on that single result.

source.guideline: ADA 2025 Section 2 (Diagnosis & Classification)
source.recommendation: In the absence of unequivocal hyperglycaemia, diagnosis requires two abnormal test results from the same sample or two separate samples; if two different tests are both above threshold the diagnosis is confirmed, if discordant repeat the abnormal test.

measuredSupports: Fasting plasma glucose (venous, lab) — LOINC 1558-6
HbA1c — LOINC 4548-4 (%) / 59261-8 (mmol/mol)
Random / casual plasma glucose — LOINC 2345-7
2-hour OGTT plasma glucose (75 g) — LOINC 1518-0
Capillary fingerstick glucose (screening/point-of-care, not confirmatory) — LOINC 41653-7
Body mass index / weight (T2DM phenotype)
Blood pressure (frequent co-morbid hypertension)
complications: Diabetic retinopathy (leading cause of preventable blindness) — dilated retinal exam
Diabetic nephropathy / chronic kidney disease — eGFR + spot urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio annually
Diabetic peripheral neuropathy and autonomic neuropathy — annual foot exam (monofilament)
Cardiovascular disease — ischaemic heart disease, myocardial infarction, stroke (macrovascular)
Hyperglycaemic hyperosmolar state (HHS); diabetic ketoacidosis less typical but possible
sourcesConsulted: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2025, Section 2 (PMC11635041)
WHO diabetes diagnostic criteria (as cited in Ugandan/WHO literature)
PLOS One 2022 Uganda HbA1c/FPG diagnostic-accuracy study (pone.0272515)
csoNotes: Confirm whether the tool should encode the Ugandan-validated lower cut-offs (FPG ~6.4 mmol/L, HbA1c ~6.3%) as an advisory flag, or strictly use WHO 7.0 / 6.5%. Recommend strict WHO thresholds with an advisory note.

Decide HbA1c availability/reliability handling: many Ugandan labs lack NGSP-certified HbA1c, and anaemia/HbS/malaria/HIV confound it — the engine should prefer plasma glucose where HbA1c is unreliable.
Confirm units convention for the UI (mmol/L is standard in Uganda).

definingCriteria.criterion: Same glucose/HbA1c diagnostic thresholds as any diabetes
definingCriteria.measure: FPG / 2-h OGTT / random glucose / HbA1c (identical biochemical cut-offs to T2DM)
definingCriteria.threshold: FPG ≥ 7.0 mmol/L (126 mg/dL); 2-h OGTT ≥ 11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL); HbA1c ≥ 6.5% (48 mmol/mol); random ≥ 11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL) + symptoms
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Diagnosis of diabetes itself is biochemically identical to T2DM — type 1 is a CLASSIFICATION on top of a confirmed diabetes diagnosis, not a separate glucose threshold. Often presents acutely with DKA at first presentation in Uganda.

source.guideline: ADA 2025 Section 2 — diagnostic glucose/HbA1c criteria are common to all diabetes; classification by aetiology
source.recommendation: Diabetes is diagnosed by the same glycaemic criteria regardless of type; type 1 vs type 2 is determined by aetiologic features, not by different glucose cut-offs.

definingCriteria.criterion: Islet autoantibodies (autoimmune marker)
definingCriteria.measure: Serum islet autoantibodies: GAD65 (most available), IA-2, ZnT8, insulin autoantibodies (IAA)
definingCriteria.threshold: Presence of ≥ 1 islet autoantibody supports autoimmune (type 1) diabetes
definingCriteria.loincHint: GAD65 Ab 13926-8; IA-2/ICA512 Ab 49053-9; ZnT8 Ab 87383-7; insulin Ab 8086-1
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Autoantibody assays are largely UNAVAILABLE in most Ugandan settings, so type 1 is frequently a CLINICAL diagnosis (young/lean, abrupt onset, ketosis/DKA-prone, insulin-dependent from outset). Note atypical phenotypes seen in sub-Saharan Africa (e.g. ketosis-prone atypical diabetes / 'Flatbush', malnutrition-related diabetes) can mimic T1DM — needs CSO input on classification logic.

source.guideline: ADA 2025 Section 2 (Type 1 diabetes — autoimmune markers)
source.recommendation: Islet autoantibodies (GAD, IA-2, ZnT8, insulin) characterise immune-mediated type 1 diabetes; their presence supports classification as type 1.

definingCriteria.criterion: C-peptide (endogenous insulin reserve)
definingCriteria.measure: Fasting or random serum/plasma C-peptide (ideally paired with concurrent glucose)
definingCriteria.threshold: Low / undetectable C-peptide (e.g. < 0.24 ng/mL / < 80 pmol/L) indicates severe insulin deficiency
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: C-peptide testing has limited availability in Uganda. When obtainable it helps distinguish insulin-deficient (type 1) from insulin-resistant/retained-secretion (type 2) cases, and identify ketosis-prone atypical diabetes; must be interpreted with a simultaneous glucose. CSO to confirm the exact cut-off to encode.

source.guideline: ADA 2025 Section 2 (C-peptide in classification)
source.recommendation: Low or undetectable C-peptide (<0.24 ng/mL / <80 pmol/L) indicates severe insulin deficiency consistent with type 1 diabetes.

measuredSupports: Plasma glucose (FPG / random) — confirms the diabetes diagnosis
HbA1c — LOINC 4548-4
Blood/urine ketones (beta-hydroxybutyrate) — ketosis-prone presentation / DKA
Venous blood gas + bicarbonate + anion gap — DKA assessment
C-peptide — LOINC 1986-9 (where available)
GAD65 / IA-2 / ZnT8 / insulin autoantibodies (where available)
complications: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) — frequent at presentation and during illness
Diabetic nephropathy / CKD — eGFR + urine ACR
sourcesConsulted: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes 2025, Section 2 (PMC11635041)
csoNotes: Type 1 is not a distinct glucose threshold — confirm the tool models it as a classification layer over a confirmed diabetes diagnosis (phenotype + ketosis + insulin dependence), with autoantibody/C-peptide as optional confirmatory inputs that are often unavailable in Uganda.
Decide how to handle ketosis-prone atypical diabetes / 'Flatbush' and malnutrition-related diabetes seen in sub-Saharan Africa, which blur the T1/T2 boundary.
Confirm whether to surface autoantibody/C-peptide cut-offs at all given low local availability, or keep them advisory-only.

definingCriteria.criterion: Confirmed diabetes (any type) by standard glycaemic criteria
definingCriteria.measure: Any one diagnostic criterion met: FPG, 2-h OGTT, HbA1c, or random glucose + symptoms (with confirmation rule)
definingCriteria.threshold: FPG ≥ 7.0 mmol/L; 2-h OGTT ≥ 11.1 mmol/L; HbA1c ≥ 6.5%; random ≥ 11.1 mmol/L + symptoms
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Prerequisite: this NCD is diagnosed diabetes PLUS at least one documented end-organ complication. In Uganda many patients present late/already complicated, so complication screening at diagnosis is essential.

source.guideline: ADA 2025 Section 2 (diabetes diagnosis), concordant with WHO
source.recommendation: Diabetes is established by the standard glycaemic criteria; 'with complications' adds documented micro- and/or macrovascular end-organ disease.

definingCriteria.criterion: Diabetic kidney disease (nephropathy)
definingCriteria.measure: Spot urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR) and/or estimated GFR
definingCriteria.threshold: uACR ≥ 30 mg/g (≥ 3 mg/mmol) on ≥ 2 of 3 samples, and/or eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73m² (persistent)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: ADA/KDIGO screen at diagnosis (T2DM) and annually. Confirm whether MoH labs report eGFR with a race-free CKD-EPI equation (KDIGO now recommends race-free). uACR may be cheaper/more available than 24h collection.

source.guideline: ADA Standards of Care 2025 — Section 11 (CKD) / Section 12; KDIGO concordant
source.recommendation: Screen for diabetic kidney disease with annual urine ACR and eGFR; persistent uACR ≥ 30 mg/g or eGFR < 60 confirms diabetic kidney disease.

definingCriteria.criterion: Diabetic retinopathy
definingCriteria.measure: Dilated fundoscopic / comprehensive retinal examination (or retinal photography)
definingCriteria.threshold: Presence of any retinopathy lesions (microaneurysms, haemorrhages, exudates, neovascularisation)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: ADA: screen at diagnosis for T2DM and within 5 years for T1DM, then every 1–2 years. Access to dilated eye exams / fundus cameras is limited in Uganda — referral pathway needed.

source.guideline: ADA Standards of Care 2025 — Section 12 (Retinopathy, Neuropathy, Foot Care)
source.recommendation: Screen for diabetic retinopathy with dilated/comprehensive eye examination; any retinopathy lesion confirms the complication.

definingCriteria.criterion: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy / foot disease
definingCriteria.measure: Annual foot exam: 10g monofilament + one of (vibration 128Hz, pinprick, ankle reflexes, temperature); inspection for ulcer/deformity
definingCriteria.threshold: Loss of protective sensation (abnormal monofilament) or other abnormal test; or active/healed foot ulcer
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Foot exam is low-cost and high-yield in Uganda where late foot ulceration/amputation is common; should be a core part of the complications screen at every review.

source.guideline: ADA Standards of Care 2025 — Section 12 (Retinopathy, Neuropathy, Foot Care)
source.recommendation: Assess all patients for distal symmetric polyneuropathy at diagnosis (T2DM) and annually using 10g monofilament plus one other modality; loss of protective sensation defines high-risk neuropathy.

definingCriteria.criterion: Macrovascular / cardiovascular complication (ASCVD)
definingCriteria.measure: Clinical diagnosis of ischaemic heart disease, prior MI, stroke/TIA, or peripheral arterial disease (history/exam/ECG/imaging)
definingCriteria.threshold: Documented atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease event or established PAD
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: No single threshold — clinical/imaging diagnosis. CSO to confirm which macrovascular events the tool should capture and whether ABPI is used locally for PAD (verified ABPI < 0.9 indicates PAD).

source.guideline: ADA Standards of Care 2025 — Section 10 (Cardiovascular Disease & Risk Management)
source.recommendation: Established ASCVD (MI, stroke, PAD) in a person with diabetes constitutes diabetes with macrovascular complications and reclassifies cardiovascular risk to very-high.

eGFR — LOINC 33914-3 / 62238-1 (race-free CKD-EPI)
Serum creatinine — LOINC 2160-0
Dilated fundoscopy / retinal photography — LOINC 32451-7
10g monofilament foot exam — LOINC 97529-8
Ankle-brachial pressure index (ABPI) for PAD
Lipid profile, blood pressure, ECG (cardiovascular risk/event workup)
HbA1c (glycaemic control driving complications) — LOINC 4548-4

Diabetic foot ulceration, infection, lower-limb amputation
Acute: DKA and hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state

csoNotes: Confirm the tool models 'diabetes with complications' as a compound state: confirmed diabetes + ≥ 1 documented end-organ complication, rather than a distinct glycaemic threshold.
Confirm thresholds for nephropathy (uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, eGFR < 60) and which eGFR equation MoH labs report (recommend race-free CKD-EPI per KDIGO).
Decide complication-screening cadence to encode (ADA: at diagnosis for T2DM, with type-specific timing for retinopathy) and the local referral pathways for eye/foot/renal where capacity is limited.
Section 10/12 thresholds for macrovascular disease are clinical, not single numeric cut-offs — confirm capture model.

https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/48/Supplement_1/S252/157552/12-Retinopathy-Neuropathy-and-Foot-Care-Standards (ADA 2025 Section 12 Retinopathy/Neuropathy/Foot Care — SEARCH-confirmed screening recs)
csoNotes: All numeric thresholds were confirmed from fetched/searched sources, not memory. The core WHO/ADA glycaemic cut-offs are fully concordant across WHO and ADA and are the criteria officially applied in Uganda.

Single most important Uganda-specific caveat for the CSO: a Ugandan diagnostic-accuracy study (PLOS One 2022) found the locally optimal cut-offs were LOWER than WHO (FPG ~6.4 mmol/L, HbA1c ~6.3%), and HbA1c is confounded by the high local prevalence of anaemia, haemoglobinopathy (HbS), malaria and HIV. Recommend the tool keep strict WHO thresholds (7.0 mmol/L / 6.5%) but flag HbA1c unreliability and prefer plasma glucose where haemoglobinopathy/anaemia is likely. CSO to ratify.

Type 1 vs Type 2 is a classification layer over a confirmed diabetes diagnosis (same glycaemic thresholds), distinguished by phenotype ± autoantibodies/C-peptide — the latter often unavailable in Uganda. Watch for ketosis-prone atypical ('Flatbush') and malnutrition-related diabetes that blur the boundary; CSO input needed on classification logic.

Could not safely confirm the standalone WHO numeric thresholds from a WHO-hosted page (the WHO fact sheet carried no numbers; the full WHO/IDF definition PDF was intentionally not fetched per the no-large-PDF rule). The WHO values are corroborated by the Ugandan literature citing WHO and by ADA concordance. If the CSO wants a primary WHO citation for the numbers, source the WHO 'Classification of diabetes mellitus 2019' or 'Definition and diagnosis of diabetes mellitus 2006' documents directly.

LOINC codes for FPG (1558-6) and HbA1c (4548-4) were source-confirmed; other LOINC hints (glucose variants, OGTT, autoantibodies, uACR/eGFR, monofilament) are provided as best-known mappings and should be validated against the project's LOINC table before encoding.

definingCriteria.criterion: Office blood pressure diagnostic threshold
definingCriteria.measure: Office systolic BP / diastolic BP (seated, validated device, average of repeat readings)
definingCriteria.threshold: Systolic ≥140 mmHg and/or diastolic ≥90 mmHg
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Aligns with the WHO/ISH ≥140/90 mmHg office threshold used in WHO-PEN and the Uganda Clinical Guidelines. In Uganda, out-of-office confirmation (ABPM/HBPM) is usually unavailable; UCG/WHO-PEN practice confirms on repeat clinic visits and uses the WHO/ISH risk chart (non-lab version applicable where cholesterol testing is absent).

source.guideline: WHO Hypertension fact sheet
source.recommendation: Hypertension is diagnosed if, when measured on two different days, systolic BP readings on both days are ≥140 mmHg and/or diastolic BP readings on both days are ≥90 mmHg.

definingCriteria.criterion: Confirmation of diagnosis (number of visits/days)
definingCriteria.measure: Repeat office BP measurement across separate occasions
definingCriteria.threshold: Confirm on ≥2 different days/visits (ISH: 2–3 visits at 1–4 week intervals); single-visit diagnosis allowed if BP ≥180/110 mmHg with evidence of CVD/target-organ damage
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: WHO requires measurement on two different days. ISH 2020 (the WHO-aligned global guideline appropriate for low-resource settings) permits single-visit diagnosis only when BP ≥180/110 mmHg with CVD evidence — directly relevant where follow-up visits are hard to guarantee.

source.guideline: 2020 International Society of Hypertension (ISH) Global Hypertension Practice Guidelines
source.recommendation: Diagnosis should not be made on a single office visit; 2–3 office visits at 1–4-week intervals are typically required. Diagnosis may be made on a single visit if BP ≥180/110 mmHg with evidence of CVD.

definingCriteria.criterion: Hypertensive emergency (severe BP elevation with acute target-organ damage)
definingCriteria.measure: Office/acute-care systolic BP / diastolic BP plus new or progressive target-organ damage
definingCriteria.threshold: SBP >180 mmHg and/or DBP >120 mmHg (AHA 2024 wording: >180/110–120 mmHg) WITH new/worsening target-organ damage. Same BP without target-organ damage = severe asymptomatic hypertension/hypertensive urgency, not emergency.
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: BP cut-off alone does not define an emergency — the discriminator is acute target-organ damage (encephalopathy, ACS, acute heart failure/pulmonary oedema, AKI, aortic dissection, eclampsia). UCG handles severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia separately (BP ≥160/110 with proteinuria or organ dysfunction). Emergencies need IV antihypertensives + ICU-level care.

source.guideline: AHA Scientific Statement: Management of Elevated Blood Pressure in the Acute Care Setting (corroborated by Merck Manual Professional)
source.recommendation: Hypertensive emergency = confirmed SBP >180 and/or DBP >120 mmHg (>180/110–120) with new or progressive target-organ damage; the same BP without target-organ damage is asymptomatic markedly elevated BP, not an emergency.

Standing BP (orthostatic check) — to detect postural drop, esp. on treatment / elderly
Heart rate / pulse — LOINC 8867-4
Home BP monitoring (HBPM) average where available — confirmatory threshold ≥135/85 mmHg (ISH)
24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring (ABPM) average where available — confirmatory threshold ≥130/80 mmHg / daytime ≥135/85 (ISH)
WHO/ISH 10-year cardiovascular risk score (lab and non-lab chart versions; non-lab version used in Uganda when cholesterol testing unavailable)
Serum creatinine + eGFR (renal target-organ assessment)
Urine dipstick / urine albumin-creatinine ratio (proteinuria, hypertensive nephropathy)
Serum potassium (baseline + monitoring on diuretics/ACEi/ARB; secondary-cause screen)
Fasting glucose / HbA1c (comorbid diabetes for risk stratification)
12-lead ECG (LVH, ischaemia, arrhythmia)
Fundoscopy (hypertensive retinopathy as target-organ damage)
complications: Stroke (ischaemic from blocked artery; haemorrhagic from burst artery)
Coronary heart disease — angina and myocardial infarction (heart attack)
Arrhythmia / irregular heartbeat (can cause sudden death)
Chronic kidney disease and kidney failure
Hypertensive emergency / encephalopathy and malignant hypertension

csoNotes: Confirm the operational confirmation pathway for the Ugandan setting: WHO says 'two different days'; ISH says 2–3 visits over 1–4 weeks. Where follow-up is unreliable, decide local rule for when a single-visit diagnosis is acceptable (we have ISH's ≥180/110 + CVD rule as the anchor).
Confirm whether the tool should drive treatment by WHO/ISH risk chart (non-lab version) vs BP threshold alone, since cholesterol testing is often unavailable in Ugandan primary care.
Hypertensive-emergency BP cut-off is a screen, not the diagnosis — ensure the UI forces documentation of target-organ damage before flagging 'emergency' vs 'severe asymptomatic HTN'.

definingCriteria.criterion: Raised total cholesterol (population/screening threshold)
definingCriteria.measure: Serum total cholesterol
definingCriteria.threshold: ≥5.0 mmol/L (≥190 mg/dl)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: WHO's standard 'raised total cholesterol' cut-off (≥5.0 mmol/L / 190 mg/dl), used in WHO Global Health Observatory and STEPS surveys including Uganda STEPS. This is a screening/epidemiological threshold; treatment decisions should follow overall CVD risk, not TC alone.

source.guideline: WHO Global Health Observatory — Raised total cholesterol (≥190 mg/dl) indicator
source.recommendation: Raised total cholesterol defined as total cholesterol ≥5.0 mmol/L or ≥190 mg/dl; this approximates an LDL-C of ≥3.5 mmol/L (≥130 mg/dl).

definingCriteria.criterion: LDL-C equivalent of raised cholesterol
definingCriteria.measure: Serum LDL cholesterol (calculated or direct)
definingCriteria.threshold: ≥3.5 mmol/L (≥130 mg/dl) approximates WHO raised-TC threshold; ESC severe single-risk-factor flag at LDL-C >4.9 mmol/L (>190 mg/dl)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: LDL-C ≥3.5 mmol/L is the WHO TC-equivalent. ESC flags LDL-C >190 mg/dl as a 'very high single risk factor' (automatically high risk). LDL-C is the primary lipid treatment target where lipids are measured.

source.guideline: WHO Global Health Observatory raised-cholesterol metadata; ESC/EAS 2019 risk-factor definition
source.recommendation: WHO: TC ≥5.0 mmol/L approximates LDL-C ≥3.5 mmol/L (130 mg/dl). ESC/EAS: LDL-C >4.9 mmol/L (>190 mg/dl) counts as a very-high single risk factor placing patient at high risk.

definingCriteria.criterion: LDL-C treatment goal — very-high CVD risk
definingCriteria.measure: Serum LDL cholesterol
definingCriteria.threshold: <1.4 mmol/L (<55 mg/dl) AND ≥50% reduction from baseline
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Very-high risk = documented ASCVD, diabetes with target-organ damage or ≥3 major risk factors, severe CKD (eGFR <30), FH with ASCVD/major risk factor, or SCORE ≥10%. Risk-stratified goals are aspirational targets; in Uganda, statin access/affordability and lipid-assay availability should be confirmed before encoding hard targets.

source.guideline: 2019 ESC/EAS Guidelines for the management of dyslipidaemias (ACC Ten Points summary)
source.recommendation: Very-high-risk: LDL-C goal <1.4 mmol/L (<55 mg/dl) and ≥50% reduction from baseline.

definingCriteria.criterion: LDL-C treatment goal — high CVD risk
definingCriteria.measure: Serum LDL cholesterol
definingCriteria.threshold: <1.8 mmol/L (<70 mg/dl) AND ≥50% reduction from baseline
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: High risk = markedly raised single risk factor (TC >310 mg/dl, LDL-C >190 mg/dl, or BP ≥180/110 mmHg), diabetes >10 years or with a major risk factor, moderate CKD (eGFR 30–59), or SCORE 5–9%.

source.guideline: 2019 ESC/EAS Guidelines for the management of dyslipidaemias (ACC Ten Points summary)
source.recommendation: High-risk: LDL-C goal <1.8 mmol/L (<70 mg/dl) and ≥50% reduction from baseline.

definingCriteria.criterion: LDL-C treatment goal — moderate CVD risk
definingCriteria.measure: Serum LDL cholesterol
definingCriteria.threshold: <2.6 mmol/L (<100 mg/dl)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Moderate risk = SCORE 1–4% (includes young T1DM <35y and T2DM <50y without other risk factors).

source.guideline: 2019 ESC/EAS Guidelines for the management of dyslipidaemias (ACC Ten Points summary)
source.recommendation: Moderate-risk: LDL-C goal <2.6 mmol/L (<100 mg/dl).

definingCriteria.criterion: LDL-C treatment goal — low CVD risk
definingCriteria.measure: Serum LDL cholesterol
definingCriteria.threshold: <3.0 mmol/L (<116 mg/dl)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Low risk = SCORE <1%. 'Consider' goal rather than a firm target.

source.guideline: 2019 ESC/EAS Guidelines for the management of dyslipidaemias (ACC Ten Points summary)
source.recommendation: Low-risk: consider LDL-C goal <3.0 mmol/L (<116 mg/dl).

definingCriteria.criterion: CVD-risk-based treatment approach (resource-appropriate)
definingCriteria.measure: 10-year total cardiovascular risk (WHO/ISH chart) combined with lipid level
definingCriteria.threshold: Statin therapy driven by overall 10-year CVD risk rather than an isolated lipid cut-off (WHO/ISH chart; non-lab chart usable when lipids unavailable)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: WHO-PEN / Uganda practice uses total-CVD-risk charts (WHO/ISH), including a non-laboratory version, because routine lipid testing is frequently unavailable in primary care. CSO should set the operational decision rule (risk-based vs threshold-based) and which chart/region calibration to embed.

source.guideline: WHO/ISH cardiovascular risk prediction charts (referenced in WHO-PEN and Uganda Clinical Guidelines)
source.recommendation: Where blood cholesterol measurement is unavailable, use the WHO/ISH non-laboratory CVD risk chart; treat based on total 10-year cardiovascular risk rather than a single lipid threshold.

Confirm which HDL/TG cut-offs to encode for the Ugandan population (the local STEPS study used HDL <1.0 men / <1.3 women, TC ≥5.2 mmol/L) vs WHO TC ≥5.0 mmol/L — minor divergence flagged.

definingCriteria.criterion: HFrEF — symptomatic HF with reduced LVEF
definingCriteria.measure: Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) on echocardiography
definingCriteria.threshold: LVEF ≤40%
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Echo confirmation requires a sonographer/cardiologist and machine — available at national/regional referral level (e.g. Mulago, UHI) but not at most HC-level facilities. At lower levels HF is a clinical/CXR diagnosis; LVEF category is assigned once echo is obtained on referral.

source.guideline: ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic heart failure (definitions reaffirmed by the 2021 Universal Definition of HF)
source.recommendation: HFrEF = symptomatic HF with LVEF ≤40%

definingCriteria.criterion: HFmrEF — symptomatic HF with mildly reduced LVEF
definingCriteria.measure: Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) on echocardiography
definingCriteria.threshold: LVEF 41–49%
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Requires echo for categorisation; same access constraints as HFrEF. ESC 2021 frames HFmrEF as a distinct category that may benefit from HFrEF-type therapy.

source.guideline: ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic heart failure / Universal Definition of HF
source.recommendation: HFmrEF = symptomatic HF with LVEF 41–49%

definingCriteria.criterion: HFpEF — symptomatic HF with preserved LVEF plus objective cardiac abnormality
definingCriteria.measure: LVEF on echo PLUS evidence of structural/functional cardiac abnormality (e.g. LV hypertrophy, left atrial enlargement, diastolic dysfunction) and/or raised natriuretic peptides
definingCriteria.threshold: LVEF ≥50% with corroborating structural/functional abnormality and/or raised NPs
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: HFpEF is the hardest to confirm in low-resource settings: needs echo (LVEF + diastolic indices/LA size) and ideally natriuretic peptide testing, both limited outside referral centres. Often a presumptive diagnosis pending referral.

source.guideline: ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic heart failure / Universal Definition of HF
source.recommendation: HFpEF = symptoms/signs of HF, LVEF ≥50%, with evidence of structural and/or functional cardiac abnormalities and/or raised natriuretic peptides

definingCriteria.criterion: NT-proBNP — rule-out / corroboration of chronic HF in ambulatory setting
definingCriteria.measure: Plasma N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP)
definingCriteria.threshold: NT-proBNP <125 pg/mL makes chronic HF unlikely; ≥125 pg/mL corroborates / triggers further evaluation
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: NT-proBNP assays are not routinely available in most Ugandan public facilities; UCG/WHO-PEN HF diagnosis is predominantly clinical (symptoms/signs) ± CXR ± echo on referral. Use NP thresholds where the assay exists (private/referral labs).

source.guideline: ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic heart failure (NP rule-out thresholds; consistent with Universal Definition 2021)
source.recommendation: NT-proBNP <125 pg/mL (ambulatory) makes a diagnosis of HF unlikely; threshold ≥125 pg/mL used for a positive/rule-in test in symptomatic patients

definingCriteria.criterion: BNP — rule-out of chronic HF in ambulatory setting
definingCriteria.measure: Plasma B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP)
definingCriteria.threshold: BNP <35 pg/mL makes chronic HF unlikely (ambulatory rule-out)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: BNP, like NT-proBNP, is largely a referral/private-lab test in Uganda; not part of standard lower-level HF workup.

source.guideline: ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic heart failure
source.recommendation: BNP <35 pg/mL in the ambulatory/non-acute setting makes a diagnosis of chronic HF unlikely

definingCriteria.criterion: HFimpEF — HF with improved ejection fraction (longitudinal category)
definingCriteria.measure: Serial LVEF on echocardiography
definingCriteria.threshold: Baseline LVEF ≤40%, a ≥10-point absolute increase from baseline, AND a second LVEF measurement >40%
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Requires repeat echo over time; feasible only where serial echo is accessible. Useful for the longitudinal record once a patient is on guideline-directed therapy.

source.guideline: Universal Definition and Classification of Heart Failure
source.recommendation: HFimpEF = symptomatic HF with baseline LVEF ≤40%, ≥10-point increase from baseline, and a second measurement of LVEF >40%

measuredSupports: Echocardiography: LVEF (category-defining), LV wall thickness/LVH, left atrial size, diastolic function indices, valve assessment, chamber dimensions
12-lead ECG (rarely entirely normal in HF; identifies AF, prior MI, LVH, conduction disease)
Chest X-ray (cardiomegaly, pulmonary congestion/oedema, pleural effusion) — key low-resource tool
Natriuretic peptides: NT-proBNP / BNP (rule-out and corroboration where available)
Serum electrolytes (Na, K), renal function/eGFR (baseline + monitoring on diuretics/RAAS inhibitors)
Full blood count (anaemia as precipitant), TSH (thyroid as precipitant), fasting glucose/HbA1c
NYHA functional class and weight/fluid-status documentation for monitoring
complications: Acute decompensated heart failure / pulmonary oedema
Atrial fibrillation and other arrhythmias; sudden cardiac death
Cardiac cachexia and progressive functional decline
csoNotes: LVEF cut-offs (≤40 / 41–49 / ≥50) are well-established and consistent across ESC 2021 and the 2021 Universal Definition — high confidence.

CSO to confirm whether the tool should expose NP thresholds at all given limited Ugandan availability, or treat HF as clinically defined with echo on referral. Consider age-adjusted NT-proBNP rule-in thresholds (≥125 / ≥250 / ≥500 pg/mL for <50 / 50–74 / ≥75 yr) if NP testing is enabled.
Confirm whether UCG specifies any local HF diagnostic pathway to anchor to (not located in this HTML search — WHO-PEN/UCG HF entry should be checked directly by CSO).

ncds.ncd: Ischaemic heart disease / Chronic coronary syndrome (CCS)

definingCriteria.criterion: Obstructive coronary artery disease — anatomical definition
definingCriteria.measure: Coronary luminal stenosis on invasive coronary angiography (ICA) or coronary CT angiography (CCTA)
definingCriteria.threshold: ≥50% diameter stenosis of an epicardial coronary artery
definingCriteria.loincHint: Imaging finding (no single universal LOINC; document via cardiac imaging report)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: ICA and CCTA are available only at the Uganda Heart Institute / national referral level; CCS in most Ugandan settings is a clinical diagnosis (typical angina) supported by ECG ± troponin to exclude ACS, with anatomical confirmation reserved for referral.

source.guideline: ESC Guidelines for the management of chronic coronary syndromes
source.recommendation: Obstructive CAD defined as ≥50% diameter stenosis on coronary angiography

definingCriteria.criterion: Functionally significant stenosis — physiological definition
definingCriteria.measure: Invasive coronary physiology: fractional flow reserve (FFR) or instantaneous wave-free ratio (iFR)
definingCriteria.threshold: FFR ≤0.80 (or iFR ≤0.89) indicates a functionally/ischaemia-significant stenosis
definingCriteria.loincHint: Procedure-derived value (catheter lab report; no standard LOINC)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Invasive physiology (FFR/iFR) is essentially unavailable outside specialist cardiac catheterisation services; relevant only for patients referred to UHI for angiography.

source.guideline: ESC Guidelines for the management of chronic coronary syndromes
source.recommendation: Assess functional severity of intermediate stenoses with FFR (significance threshold ≤0.80) or iFR (≤0.89) before revascularisation

definingCriteria.criterion: Pre-test / clinical likelihood of obstructive CAD — diagnostic triage thresholds
definingCriteria.measure: Risk-factor-weighted clinical likelihood model (age, sex, symptom type + risk factors)
definingCriteria.threshold: Very low ≤5% (defer further testing); low >5–15% (consider coronary artery calcium scoring); higher likelihood → non-invasive imaging or ICA
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: The CACS pathway and many non-invasive functional tests are not widely available; the clinical likelihood concept (typical vs atypical angina by age/sex) is still useful for prioritising referral. Treat exact % bands as decision-support, not hard gates, in the Ugandan context.

source.guideline: ESC Guidelines for the management of chronic coronary syndromes
source.recommendation: Use a risk-factor-weighted clinical likelihood model; defer testing if very low (≤5%); consider CACS for low (>5–15%) likelihood

measuredSupports: 12-lead ECG at rest (resting changes, Q waves of prior MI, ST/T abnormalities) and during symptoms
Troponin (high-sensitivity where available) — to distinguish CCS from acute coronary syndrome
Echocardiography (resting LV function, regional wall-motion abnormalities, alternative causes of chest pain)
Non-invasive ischaemia/anatomy testing where available: CCTA, stress echo, stress ECG, SPECT/MPI, stress CMR
Coronary artery calcium score (CACS) for reclassification in low likelihood patients
Lipid profile (LDL-C), HbA1c/fasting glucose, blood pressure, renal function — cardiovascular risk factor assessment
Invasive coronary angiography ± FFR/iFR at referral level
complications: Acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina, NSTEMI, STEMI)
Acute myocardial infarction and its mechanical complications (papillary muscle rupture, VSD, free-wall rupture)
Ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death
Mural thrombus and systemic thromboembolism / ischaemic stroke
csoNotes: Anatomical (≥50% stenosis) and physiological (FFR ≤0.80 / iFR ≤0.89) definitions are firm ESC 2024 numbers — high confidence.

Pre-test likelihood % bands marked medium confidence: the 2024 model is risk-factor-weighted and the exact bands matter mainly where CACS/non-invasive testing exists; in Uganda most diagnosis is clinical + ECG/troponin. CSO to decide how much of the ESC triage pathway to surface.

No Uganda-specific IHD/CCS diagnostic threshold document was located via HTML search — CSO should confirm against UCG/WHO-PEN CVD risk pathway. The tool should keep CCS as decision-support and route suspected ACS to emergency pathways, not the CCS pathway.

definingCriteria.criterion: Reduced GFR persisting ≥3 months
definingCriteria.measure: Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), creatinine-based (CKD-EPI), ideally with cystatin C confirmation
definingCriteria.threshold: eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m² present for ≥3 months
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Serum creatinine is widely available; eGFR should be calculated with a race-free equation. Note CKD-EPI was derived largely in non-African populations — interpret borderline eGFR with caution in Ugandan patients. The ≥3-month persistence (repeat testing) is essential and frequently missed where follow-up is hard; avoid labelling AKI as CKD on a single value.

source.guideline: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
source.recommendation: CKD = abnormalities of kidney structure or function present for ≥3 months; GFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m² qualifies as a marker of decreased function

definingCriteria.criterion: Albuminuria as a marker of kidney damage persisting ≥3 months
definingCriteria.measure: Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR), preferably first-morning void
definingCriteria.threshold: ACR ≥30 mg/g (≥3 mg/mmol) for ≥3 months (qualifies as CKD even if eGFR ≥60)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Quantitative ACR is often unavailable at lower-level facilities; urine dipstick proteinuria is the common surrogate but is less sensitive for moderately increased albuminuria (A2) and should be confirmed with ACR where possible. Persistence (≥3 months) again required.

source.guideline: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
source.recommendation: Albuminuria (ACR ≥30 mg/g [≥3 mg/mmol]) is a marker of kidney damage; its persistence ≥3 months defines CKD independent of GFR

definingCriteria.criterion: GFR category staging (G1–G5)
definingCriteria.measure: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m²)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: G1/G2 are only CKD when accompanied by another marker of kidney damage (e.g. albuminuria, structural abnormality). G5 (<15) defines kidney failure; dialysis/transplant access is very limited in Uganda, making early staging and prevention especially important.

source.guideline: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease

definingCriteria.criterion: Albuminuria category staging (A1–A3)
definingCriteria.measure: Urine ACR
definingCriteria.threshold: A1 <30 mg/g (<3 mg/mmol); A2 30–300 mg/g (3–30 mg/mmol); A3 >300 mg/g (>30 mg/mmol)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Combine with GFR category for the CGA (Cause–GFR–Albuminuria) risk grid that drives the KDIGO green/yellow/orange/red risk heat-map. Note: one source rendered the A3 SI cut-off ambiguously; the standard A3 is >300 mg/g i.e. >30 mg/mmol.

source.guideline: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
source.recommendation: Albuminuria categories: A1 <30 mg/g, A2 30–300 mg/g, A3 >300 mg/g (SI: <3, 3–30, >30 mg/mmol)

definingCriteria.criterion: Classification framework (CGA) and confirmation requirement
definingCriteria.measure: Cause + GFR category + Albuminuria category; diagnosis confirmed by repeat testing
definingCriteria.threshold: Diagnosis cannot be made on a single test — confirm by repeat testing over ≥3 months (or nephrology input for suspected advanced CKD)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Stress the confirmation step in the tool to avoid mislabelling transient/AKI changes as CKD where follow-up is logistically hard.

source.guideline: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
source.recommendation: Classify CKD by Cause, GFR (G1–G5) and Albuminuria (A1–A3); a diagnosis requires abnormalities persisting ≥3 months (repeat testing).

measuredSupports: Serum creatinine → eGFR (CKD-EPI; cystatin C confirmation where available)
Urine ACR (preferred) or urine dipstick proteinuria as surrogate
Urinalysis / urine microscopy (haematuria, casts, sediment abnormalities)
Renal ultrasound (kidney size, echogenicity, obstruction, polycystic disease)
Serum electrolytes (K, Na, bicarbonate/acidosis), calcium, phosphate
Haemoglobin/FBC (anaemia of CKD), PTH and vitamin D (mineral-bone disease)
Blood pressure and HbA1c/fasting glucose (hypertension and diabetes as leading causes/drivers)
complications: Progression to kidney failure (G5 / end-stage kidney disease) requiring dialysis or transplant
Cardiovascular disease (leading cause of death in CKD; accelerated atherosclerosis, LVH, heart failure)
CKD–mineral and bone disorder (hyperphosphataemia, secondary hyperparathyroidism, renal osteodystrophy, vascular calcification)
Volume overload / resistant hypertension / pulmonary oedema
Increased susceptibility to drug toxicity / need for renal dose adjustment
csoNotes: GFR/albuminuria categories and the ≥3-month rule are firmly confirmed from the KDIGO 2024 primer — high confidence on all numbers.

One fetched source displayed the A3 SI value as '>300 mg/mmol' which is a typographical error; standard KDIGO A3 = >300 mg/g = >30 mg/mmol. Flagged for CSO; recommend the tool encode A3 as >300 mg/g (>30 mg/mmol).
Recommend the tool surface the confirmation/persistence requirement and the AKI-vs-CKD distinction, given Ugandan follow-up constraints; and use a race-free eGFR equation.

All thresholds were fetched/searched live (no memory): HF LVEF cut-offs and NP rule-out values from ESC 2021 / 2021 Universal Definition; CCS anatomical (≥50% stenosis) and physiological (FFR ≤0.80 / iFR ≤0.89) definitions from ESC 2024; CKD eGFR/ACR/category thresholds from the KDIGO 2024 guideline primer.

No Uganda-specific (UCG / WHO-PEN) threshold document was successfully located via HTML search within the fetch budget — all defining numbers anchor to the named specialty guidelines (ESC, KDIGO). CSO should verify against the current Uganda Clinical Guidelines NCD chapter and WHO-PEN, particularly for which investigations are realistically available at each Ugandan facility level.

Recurring Ugandan-context theme across all three NCDs: the category-defining investigations (echo/LVEF, NP assays, coronary angiography/FFR, quantitative ACR, cystatin C) are concentrated at national/referral level. The tool should let lower-level facilities record a presumptive clinical diagnosis and assign the formal category/stage once referral-level testing is obtained.
A large guideline PDF for the ESC HF (Wiley full text) returned HTTP 402 and was abandoned per instructions; ACC summary pages were used to confirm the same numbers instead.

definingCriteria.criterion: Persistent airflow limitation confirmed by spirometry
definingCriteria.measure: Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio
definingCriteria.threshold: < 0.70 (fixed ratio)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Spirometry is frequently unavailable at lower-level Ugandan facilities; UCG/WHO-PEN allow a presumptive clinical diagnosis (chronic cough/dyspnoea + exposure: biomass smoke, tobacco) but the FEV1/FVC<0.70 fixed ratio remains the confirmatory standard where spirometry exists. Flag spirometry availability as a CSO/site question.

source.guideline: GOLD (Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease) — Spirometry Quick Guide
source.recommendation: "The spirometric criterion required for a diagnosis of COPD is an FEV1/FVC ratio below 0.7 after bronchodilator." Pre-BD spirometry used to rule out COPD; post-BD confirms it.

definingCriteria.criterion: Appropriate symptoms plus risk exposure (diagnosis is not spirometry alone)
definingCriteria.measure: Chronic dyspnoea, cough, sputum + significant exposure (tobacco, biomass/HAP)
definingCriteria.threshold: Symptoms + exposure must accompany FEV1/FVC<0.70; spirometry mandatory to establish diagnosis
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Biomass/household air pollution is a major COPD driver in Uganda (cooking smoke), not only tobacco — capture this exposure explicitly.

source.guideline: GOLD — Spirometry Quick Guide / Science Committee recommendations
source.recommendation: COPD diagnosis requires post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC<0.70 PLUS appropriate symptoms and significant exposure to noxious stimuli; clinical symptoms alone are insufficient.

definingCriteria.criterion: Severity grading of airflow limitation (GOLD grade)
definingCriteria.measure: Post-bronchodilator FEV1 % predicted (in patients with FEV1/FVC<0.70)
definingCriteria.threshold: GOLD 1 (mild) FEV1 ≥ 80%; GOLD 2 (moderate) 50–79%; GOLD 3 (severe) 30–49%; GOLD 4 (very severe) < 30%
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Severity grade only applies once FEV1/FVC<0.70 confirms obstruction. Not retrievable from the small Quick Guide page fetched; these are the long-standing GOLD 1-4 % predicted cut-points and should be CSO-confirmed against the current GOLD report.

source.guideline: GOLD — Global Strategy for Diagnosis, Management and Prevention of COPD
source.recommendation: Spirometric severity (GOLD grades 1–4) defined by post-bronchodilator FEV1 % predicted thresholds 80/50/30%.

measuredSupports: Spirometry: post-BD FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC ratio (diagnostic + grading)
FEV1 % predicted (severity grade)
SpO2 / pulse oximetry (assess hypoxaemia, screen for need for ABG / oxygen)
mMRC dyspnoea scale and CAT score (symptom burden — drives GOLD ABE group)
Exacerbation history in past 12 months (risk stratification)
Chest X-ray (exclude alternatives: TB, cardiomegaly, mass — high TB prevalence in Uganda)
BMI / weight (cachexia is prognostic)
complications: Cor pulmonale / pulmonary hypertension and right heart failure
sourcesConsulted: GOLD Science Committee pre-/post-bronchodilator spirometry recommendations (search) — https://publications.ersnet.org/content/erj/65/2/2401603
csoNotes: Confirm whether the tool should permit a presumptive clinical COPD label where spirometry is unavailable (common in Uganda), and how to surface 'spirometry not done' vs 'FEV1/FVC<0.70 confirmed'.
Confirm GOLD 1–4 FEV1 %-predicted cut-points (80/50/30) against the current GOLD report — taken from GOLD's standing grading, not from the small page fetched.
Capture biomass/household-air-pollution exposure as a first-class risk factor, not just tobacco.

definingCriteria.criterion: Documented variable expiratory airflow limitation (NOT a single fixed threshold) plus a history of variable respiratory symptoms
definingCriteria.measure: Demonstrated variability in lung function (spirometry or PEF), combined with characteristic symptom pattern (wheeze, breathlessness, chest tightness, cough — variable over time and in intensity)
definingCriteria.threshold: No single cut-off: diagnosis requires (a) history of variable symptoms AND (b) documented variable airflow limitation by at least one objective test below
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: GINA explicitly states there is no single 'gold-standard' test. Where spirometry is unavailable in Uganda, serial PEF over 2 weeks (best of 3 readings, morning + evening) is the practical objective test. Asthma is under-diagnosed in LMICs.

source.guideline: GINA (Global Initiative for Asthma) Strategy / 2024 Summary Guide
source.recommendation: "No single test serves as a 'gold-standard' test for asthma diagnosis"; diagnosis rests on documented variability rather than fixed thresholds alone.

definingCriteria.criterion: Positive bronchodilator reversibility test
definingCriteria.measure: Increase in FEV1 (or FVC) 10–15 min after 200–400 mcg inhaled salbutamol
definingCriteria.threshold: Adults: increase ≥ 12% AND ≥ 200 mL from baseline (or PEF ≥ 20%). Children: increase > 12% of predicted FEV1 (some sources > 15%)
definingCriteria.loincHint: FEV1 19911-7; bronchodilator response FEV1 % change 52485-0; PEF 19935-6
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Bronchodilator reversibility has high specificity but low sensitivity (may be absent at a single visit because asthma is variable) — a negative test does not exclude asthma.

source.guideline: GINA (Global Initiative for Asthma) — diagnostic criteria for variable airflow limitation
source.recommendation: Positive bronchodilator reversibility in adults = FEV1 (or FVC) increase ≥ 12% and ≥ 200 mL over baseline (PEF ≥ 20%); children ≥ 12% predicted.

definingCriteria.criterion: Excessive average daily diurnal PEF variability
definingCriteria.measure: Twice-daily peak expiratory flow (PEF) charting, averaged over 1–2 weeks
definingCriteria.threshold: Adults: average daily diurnal PEF variability > 10%. Children: > 13%
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: PEF meters are low-cost and the most deployable objective test in Ugandan primary care where spirometry is scarce — likely the default variability test in the tool.

source.guideline: GINA (Global Initiative for Asthma) — diagnostic criteria
source.recommendation: Excessive average daily diurnal PEF variability supporting asthma = > 10% in adults, > 13% in children.

definingCriteria.criterion: Demonstrated airflow limitation at presentation (supports diagnosis; reduced ratio)
definingCriteria.measure: FEV1/FVC ratio when symptomatic
definingCriteria.threshold: Reduced FEV1/FVC (below lower limit of normal; GINA notes <0.75–0.80 in adults, <0.90 in children) documents airflow limitation that should then be shown to be variable
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: A reduced FEV1/FVC documents obstruction but does not by itself diagnose asthma — variability/reversibility must also be shown. Do not hard-code a single ratio cut-off.

source.guideline: GINA (Global Initiative for Asthma) — diagnostic criteria for airflow limitation
source.recommendation: GINA recommends documenting expiratory airflow limitation by a reduced FEV1/FVC (below LLN; commonly <0.75–0.80 in adults) before establishing variability.

definingCriteria.criterion: Significant improvement in lung function after a trial of anti-inflammatory (controller) treatment
definingCriteria.measure: FEV1 change after 4 weeks of inhaled corticosteroid treatment
definingCriteria.threshold: Adults: FEV1 increase > 12% and > 200 mL (or PEF > 20%) from baseline after 4 weeks of controller treatment, outside respiratory infections
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Useful confirmatory route when initial spirometry/PEF is non-diagnostic but clinical suspicion is high.

source.guideline: GINA (Global Initiative for Asthma) — diagnostic criteria
source.recommendation: Significant increase in lung function (FEV1 >12% and >200 mL, or PEF >20%) after 4 weeks of anti-inflammatory treatment supports the diagnosis.

measuredSupports: Spirometry: FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC, pre/post-bronchodilator (reversibility)
Peak expiratory flow (PEF) — single value and 1–2 week diurnal variability chart
FeNO (fractional exhaled nitric oxide) where available — supportive, not diagnostic
Symptom-control tools: ACT / GINA symptom-control assessment
SpO2 / pulse oximetry during acute exacerbation
Allergy / atopy markers (eosinophils, total/specific IgE) — supportive of phenotype
Trigger and exposure history (allergens, biomass smoke, occupational)
complications: Acute severe asthma / status asthmaticus (life-threatening exacerbation)
Airway remodelling with fixed (persistent) airflow limitation
Inhaled-corticosteroid side effects (oral candidiasis, dysphonia); systemic steroid effects with frequent courses
Impaired quality of life, sleep disturbance, missed school/work, death from severe attack
sourcesConsulted: BTS/NICE/SIGN guideline for asthma 2024 vs GINA 2024 comparison, PMC (fetched) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11992161/
GINA Summary Guide for Asthma Management and Prevention 2024 (search) — https://ginasthma.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/GINA-Summary-Guide-2024-WEB-WMS.pdf
Key recommendations for primary care from the 2022 GINA update, npj PCRM / PMC (search) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9907191/
DrOracle GINA adult asthma diagnostic criteria summary (search) — https://www.droracle.ai/articles/3431/what-are-the-diagnostic-criteria-for-adult-asthma-according
csoNotes: By design there is NO single asthma threshold — the tool must model asthma as 'history of variable symptoms + at least one documented objective variability test', not a numeric cut-off. Confirm this framing.
Confirm the children's bronchodilator reversibility figure (>12% predicted per GINA adult/paeds; some summaries cite >15% in children) and whether the tool is adult-only.
Reduced FEV1/FVC cut-offs (<0.75–0.80 adults) are guidance, not a hard diagnostic line — verify wording with CSO before encoding.
Given Uganda spirometry scarcity, decide whether serial PEF variability is the primary objective test in the workflow.

definingCriteria.criterion: Acute focal (or global) neurological deficit of presumed vascular origin
definingCriteria.measure: Clinical: sudden-onset focal neurological dysfunction (e.g., FAST — Face/Arm/Speech, hemiparesis, dysphasia, visual loss); WHO classic definition = rapidly developing signs of focal/global cerebral disturbance lasting >24 h (or leading to death) with no apparent cause other than vascular origin
definingCriteria.threshold: Sudden focal neuro deficit, vascular in origin; persisting >24 h distinguishes stroke from TIA (TIA = transient deficit resolving without infarction)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Clinical recognition (FAST / sudden focal deficit) drives the pathway in Ugandan facilities where imaging access is limited; UCG/WHO-PEN emphasise rapid referral. Onset time is critical for thrombolysis eligibility.

source.guideline: WHO Stroke fact sheet (News-room)
source.recommendation: "A stroke is a medical emergency that occurs when blood flow to the brain is interrupted, either due to a blockage or bleeding." Acute focal/global neurological dysfunction of vascular cause.

definingCriteria.criterion: Neuroimaging to confirm stroke and classify subtype (ischaemic vs haemorrhagic)
definingCriteria.measure: Non-contrast brain CT (or MRI) as soon as possible
definingCriteria.threshold: Imaging required to (a) confirm stroke, (b) distinguish ischaemic (infarction) from haemorrhagic (intracerebral/subarachnoid haemorrhage) — these are mutually exclusive categories (plus 'undetermined'). Non-contrast CT is the primary modality to differentiate the two; CT haemorrhage = hyperdensity, early ischaemia may be subtle/normal
definingCriteria.loincHint: CT head w/o contrast 30799-1 (or 24725-4 CT head); MRI brain 24590-2
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: CT/MRI is often unavailable or delayed in Uganda; subtype confirmation may not be possible at first contact. The tool should explicitly support 'clinical stroke, subtype unconfirmed (no imaging)' and gate thrombolysis/aspirin decisions on imaging having excluded haemorrhage. Antiplatelets/thrombolysis must NOT be started until haemorrhage is excluded.

definingCriteria.criterion: Subclinical hypothyroidism
definingCriteria.measure: Serum TSH (elevated) with free T4 (FT4) within reference range
definingCriteria.threshold: TSH above the upper reference limit (commonly ~4.5 mIU/L) up to 10 mIU/L, AND normal free T4
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Diagnose only when thyroid function is stable, HPT axis intact and no acute severe illness (sick-euthyroid mimics). TSH upper limit depends on the local assay reference range — Ugandan labs should use their own assay ULN rather than a fixed 4.5. Confirm with a repeat after weeks before labelling.

source.guideline: AACE/ATA Clinical Practice Guidelines for Hypothyroidism in Adults
source.recommendation: Subclinical hypothyroidism = serum TSH above the upper reference limit with a normal free T4, when thyroid function is stable

definingCriteria.criterion: Subclinical hypothyroidism severity grading (mild vs severe)
definingCriteria.measure: Serum TSH
definingCriteria.threshold: Mild/Grade 1 = TSH 4.5–9.9 mIU/L; Severe/Grade 2 = TSH ≥10 mIU/L (with normal FT4)
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: TSH ≥10 mIU/L (with normal FT4) is the threshold above which levothyroxine is generally recommended even when subclinical, and the level carrying higher progression risk to overt disease.

source.guideline: StatPearls — Subclinical Hypothyroidism (NCBI Bookshelf), citing AACE/ATA practice
source.recommendation: TSH <10 vs ≥10 mIU/L distinguishes mild from severe subclinical hypothyroidism; treat when TSH >10 mIU/L

definingCriteria.criterion: Overt (primary) hypothyroidism
definingCriteria.measure: Serum TSH (elevated) with free T4 (FT4) below reference range
definingCriteria.threshold: Elevated TSH (usually >10 mIU/L) AND a subnormal (low) free T4
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Central hypothyroidism (low/normal TSH with low FT4) is the exception — do not rely on TSH alone if pituitary/hypothalamic disease is suspected; measure FT4. In Uganda, also consider iodine status and post-thyroidectomy/post-radioiodine causes.

source.guideline: AACE/ATA Clinical Practice Guidelines for Hypothyroidism in Adults
source.recommendation: Overt hypothyroidism = elevated TSH (usually >10 mIU/L) with a subnormal free T4

measuredSupports: Free T4 (FT4) — the key discriminator subclinical vs overt — LOINC 3024-7

Total T3 / free T3 (limited diagnostic value in hypothyroidism)

source.recommendation: Subclinical hyperthyroidism = low/undetectable TSH with normal free T4 and T3; treat persistent TSH <0.1 mU/L in high-risk patients

definingCriteria.criterion: Pathological mitral regurgitation (all 4 Doppler criteria required)
definingCriteria.measure: Color/continuous-wave Doppler of mitral regurgitation jet
definingCriteria.threshold: Seen in 2 views; jet length ≥2 cm in at least 1 view; peak velocity ≥3 m/s for one complete envelope; pansystolic jet in at least one envelope
definingCriteria.loincHint: Echocardiography study (no discrete LOINC for each Doppler criterion)

definingCriteria.criterion: Pathological aortic regurgitation (all 4 Doppler criteria required)
definingCriteria.measure: Color/continuous-wave Doppler of aortic regurgitation jet
definingCriteria.threshold: Seen in 2 views; jet length ≥1 cm in at least 1 view; peak velocity ≥3 m/s in early diastole; pandiastolic jet in at least one envelope

source.guideline: World Heart Federation criteria for echocardiographic diagnosis of RHD
source.recommendation: Pathological AR requires all four Doppler criteria (2 views, ≥1 cm jet, ≥3 m/s, pandiastolic)

definingCriteria.criterion: Morphological mitral valve features of RHD
definingCriteria.measure: 2D echocardiography of mitral valve
definingCriteria.threshold: Anterior mitral valve leaflet (AMVL) thickening ≥3 mm (age-specific: ≥3 mm if ≤20y, ≥4 mm if 21–40y, ≥5 mm if >40y); chordal thickening; restricted leaflet motion; excessive/prolapsing leaflet tip motion during systole
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Use age-adjusted AMVL thickness cutoffs. ≥2 morphological MV features define key categories below.

source.guideline: World Heart Federation criteria for echocardiographic diagnosis of RHD
source.recommendation: Morphological MV features: AMVL thickening (age-specific, base ≥3 mm), chordal thickening, restricted motion, excessive tip motion

definingCriteria.criterion: Mitral stenosis (mean pressure gradient)
definingCriteria.measure: Continuous-wave Doppler mean diastolic gradient across mitral valve
definingCriteria.threshold: Mean gradient ≥4 mmHg
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: MS with mean gradient ≥4 mmHg is one of the 'definite RHD' qualifying lesions.

source.guideline: World Heart Federation criteria for echocardiographic diagnosis of RHD
source.recommendation: Mitral stenosis with mean gradient ≥4 mmHg qualifies as definite RHD

definingCriteria.criterion: Definite RHD (any one of the qualifying combinations)
definingCriteria.measure: Composite echocardiographic classification
definingCriteria.threshold: (a) Pathological MR + ≥2 morphological MV features; OR (b) mitral stenosis mean gradient ≥4 mmHg; OR (c) pathological AR + ≥2 morphological aortic valve features; OR (d) borderline disease of BOTH mitral and aortic valves
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: 100% specific in low-prevalence populations; the actionable category for confirming RHD in Ugandan screening/clinical practice.

source.guideline: World Heart Federation criteria for echocardiographic diagnosis of RHD
source.recommendation: Definite RHD = pathological MR+≥2 MV features, or MS ≥4 mmHg, or pathological AR+≥2 AV features, or borderline disease of both valves

definingCriteria.criterion: Borderline RHD (applies to age ≤20 years; any one)
definingCriteria.measure: Composite echocardiographic classification
definingCriteria.threshold: (a) ≥2 morphological MV features WITHOUT pathological MR or MS; OR (b) pathological MR alone; OR (c) pathological AR alone
definingCriteria.ugandaNote: Borderline category is intended for individuals ≤20 years (latent/subclinical disease); requires follow-up echo. Confirm with CSO how MedSync should track/flag borderline cases for re-screening.

source.guideline: World Heart Federation criteria for echocardiographic diagnosis of RHD
source.recommendation: Borderline RHD = ≥2 MV morphological features without pathological MR/MS, or pathological MR alone, or pathological AR alone
